title: The Mind Landscape of Xie Youyu (Youyu qiu he 幼輿丘壑)

highlight.text: The present picture was made in my early years; it does not reveal great strength of the brush; yet, it has something of the spirit of antiquity.
highlight.lead: Zhao, inscribing one of his early paintings years later:

source.author: Zhao Mengfu (Chao Meng-fu)
source.title: Colophon on one of his early paintings
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II (The Medici Society, 1933; Internet Archive scan)

work.text: One of his most celebrated landscape paintings is exhibited at the Princeton University Art Museum with the title “The Mind Landscape of Xie Youyu” (幼輿丘壑), an allusion to the nature-loving scholar-official Xie Youyu (280–322).
In early life we are told that “he did not give much attention to painting; but when with friends, he would take a sheet of paper and amuse himself by producing trees or rocks as called for.”

source.author: Herbert A. Giles
source.title: An Introduction to the History of Chinese Pictorial Art

moment.text: In painting he swept away the formal conventions of the Southern Sung Academy of Painting and restored freedom to artists.

source.author: John C. Ferguson
source.title: Chinese Painting
source.publisher: University of Chicago Press (Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: However, in 2019 Dutch scholar Lennert Gesterkamp argued that the colophon attached to the painting and mentioning Xie Youyu is a forgery, and that in fact Zhao Mengfu's intention was to honor his own spiritual master, Daoist scholar Du Daojian (1237–1318), who also celebrated nature.
